name: AKU Celebrates Its First Cohort of Early-Career Researchers

content.text: A key initiative under AKU's Research Strategic Plan, the RISE Programme is a longitudinal, mentored research leadership academy designed to equip emerging scholars with the skills and support needed to excel in grant writing, research leadership, and international collaboration. Throughout the closing week, participants engaged in high-impact discussions, refined their research proposals, and received expert mentorship to enhance their competitiveness for international grants.

The programme's final sessions featured insightful addresses from university leaders, including a virtual session by AKU Provost Dr Tania Bubela and a discussion on research leadership led by Vice Provost, Research, Dr Salim Virani. Dr Nasia Safdar shared key insights on mentorship, while scholars participated in mock grant proposal presentations, receiving constructive feedback from senior faculty and peers. A highlight of the event was a meeting with the AKU President, where participants discussed the Chancellor's vision of AKU as a research-led university and their role in achieving this goal.

As the RISE scholars transition to securing international research grants, they have six months to submit proposals to competitive funding agencies. To support this, AKU's Research Office has introduced a Professional Development Fund to support each proposal submitted for a grant call, further strengthening the University's commitment to research excellence.

One of RISE's early success stories is Dr Sana Sheikh, Assistant Professor at AKU's Department of Medicine, who recently secured the Wellcome Trust Discovery Scheme Early Career Award for her research on Karachi's food streets. She credits RISE for its structured mentorship and support in navigating the complexities of the grant application process.

"The Academy refines your work, but a committed mentor is crucial. RISE's support was key in securing my Wellcome Trust grant and ensuring my research on dietary behavior in Karachi gained global recognition," said Dr Sheikh.

The Research Office remains committed to empowering early-career researchers at AKU and looks forward to celebrating the continued successes of RISE Programme participants while welcoming the next cohort of scholars.

content.title: AKU Celebrates Its First Cohort of Early-Career Researchers
content.author: Ambreen Nadeem
content.description: The Aga Khan University's (AKU) Research Initiative for Scholars Excellence (RISE) Programme marked a major milestone with the conclusion of its inaugural cohort during a closing week from January 28-31, 2025. The event, held at AKU's Karachi campus, brought together 20 early-career researchers from Pakistan and East Africa, celebrating their achievements and preparing them for the next phase of their research journey.
